## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
The curve is FLAT across N at every death rate, with no knee at the L2→DRAM spill (N≈61680). At q=0.01, ns/p dips from 8.814 (N=4000) to 8.164 (N=262000) then rises to 8.738 (N=4000000) — a shallow U with no spill-induced jump. The L1d spill at N≈963 lies below the smallest measured point. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: q=0.05 floors at ~8.7 ns/p, q=0.25 at ~11.3 ns/p. Small N shows mild overhead amortization.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 8.33 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 — 33% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. The algo is compute-bound at large N, overhead-bound at small N, never bandwidth-bound. Death rate degrades monotonically: q=0.05 peaks at 7.78 GB/s (31%), q=0.25 at 6.03 GB/s (24%). The floor rises 38% from q=0.01 to q=0.25, driven by branchy respawn cost rather than by N.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized component-wise within one particle, not across particles. The update loop loads a particle via `ldr q7`, `ldr d16`, `ldr s6`, packs components with `ext.16b v17, v7, v16, #0xc` and `mov.s v17[3], v6[0]`, then applies `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` and `str q6`. A `ld1.s {v16}[1], [x11]` indexed load gathers one element into a lane — a per-particle gather defeating streaming. The scatter section is scalar: 19 `strb` byte stores, 20 `csel`, 32 `b` with saturating clamp. Component-wise vec explains contiguous 68-byte loads, but the gather and byte-granular scatter cap throughput at 33%.

## Verdict
Refuted — at q=0.01 the algo sustains 8.33 GB/s = 33% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling, never approaching streaming. The compiler did vectorize (`fmul.4s`, `fadd.4s`), but the `ld1.s` gather and 19 `strb` scatter stores prevent streaming regardless of death rate. The 8.164 ns/p floor is 3× the bandwidth-implied 2.7 ns/p (68 bytes ÷ 25.22 GB/s), confirming compute-bound execution.
